title: HumanCLAW Asks Whether Vision-Language Models Can Act Through a Body
summary: When an embodied task fails it is usually impossible to tell whether the vision-language model chose badly or the low-level controller simply could not execute the choice. HumanCLAW decouples the two: an off-the-shelf VLM issues one atomic skill command per step, and that command is translated into a sub-second chunk of continuous full-body motion with real physical consequences including gravity and collisions. The 18-author framework evaluates decision quality separately from motor competence.
whyItMatters: Embodied benchmarks have been scoring the model and the controller as one number, which makes their results nearly uninterpretable. Harnessing the body so that every command executes as physically-consequential motion isolates the decision — the first clean answer to whether a VLM's failures are cognitive or mechanical.
